open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict identity and creation
open_points.text: “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions” because those TrialExecutions have newly minted identities.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created from the newly run TrialExecutions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not attach the new executions to it
Create a new AdmissionVerdict observation for each admission run
Replace or revise the existing verdict so it covers the new executions
open_points.default_guess: Create a new AdmissionVerdict observation for each admission run.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can have different results as binding state changes?
options: The complete result content identifies it, so one flow version may yield several ProofResult values
The flow version identifies one ProofResult whose facts change on recomputation
The proof records the dependency-state snapshot, and that snapshot participates in its identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat each complete computed result as a value, allowing different ProofResult values for the same flow version.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: The model says “Identity: value,” but its evidence says “an attempt's record is issued once,” and other issued execution observations and attempts are entities.
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution a content-substitutable value or an issued entity identified by its run, node, map index and attempt number?
options: A value identified from all of its immutable facts
An entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number
An entity with a separately minted identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number.

open_points.subject: Automatic admission and implementation activation provenance
open_points.text: M27 says “the request that caused it is told by ... the implementation's submitted_by,” while M05 says equal code for the same contract version is the same implementation and M09 allows activation on submission “new or reused.”
open_points.question: When an agent resubmits an existing implementation, which model records the agent whose current request caused the new admission executions and activation, rather than the implementation's original submitter?
options: Add the requesting actor to the admission or activation record
Create a separate implementation-submission record for every submission
Do not retain the causal requester for resubmissions
open_points.default_guess: Create a submission record for every submission and link the admission and activation to it.

open_points.subject: Read-only FlowActivation provenance
open_points.text: The action says an “agent or owner asks” to activate a flow, while M18 and M27 record the kernel as activated_by for a proven read-only flow and name no record that retains who asked.
open_points.question: Must a read-only flow activation retain the owner or agent whose request caused the kernel's automatic activation, and if so, where is that actor recorded?
options: Carry both the kernel activator and the requesting actor on FlowActivation
Retain only the kernel actor and discard the requester
open_points.default_guess: Carry the requesting actor on FlowActivation in addition to activated_by=kernel.
